rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Nothing the user started is tied to a UI surface" / NATIVE-AGENTS §6 the log is the transcript; a queue that only pops a matching head is not a queue
summary: `pending_claude_inputs` is only drained while the front entry's turn matches the turn that just started, so one entry whose `TurnStarted` never lands blocks the deque forever: every later user prompt is accepted and sent to Claude but never recorded in the transcript, and the deque grows without bound.
failure_scenario: Claude thread with a resume cursor. `send("one")` enqueues `(T1, "one")` and Claude's mapper emits `TurnStarted{T1}`; the event task's `apply_provider_event_locked` fails to persist it (`store.append` returns ENOSPC, or the reducer rejects it) and the loop only logs `"dropped invalid native-agent provider event"` (manager.rs:946-948), so nothing drains. The provider then exits, `inflight_turn` is cleared (manager.rs:1031-1039) but the deque is not. The user sends `"two"`; `resume_if_stopped` brings the thread back, a fresh `T2` is allocated, and `TurnStarted{T2}` arrives. The drain sees front `(T1, "one")` != `T2`, pops nothing, and `"two"` is sent to Claude but never appears as a `UserMessage` item — the transcript shows the model answering a prompt that is not there, and `(T1, "one")` stays queued for the life of the daemon.
proposed_fix: Drain by turn rather than by head: `state.pending_claude_inputs.retain(...)` / `extract_if` on `pending_turn == turn`, and drop entries for a turn once `inflight_turn` is cleared at manager.rs:1031-1039 (the same place `TurnCompleted`/`TurnAborted`/`SessionExited`/fatal `RuntimeError` already reset it), logging what was discarded.
test_plan: Add to `manager/tests.rs` beside `send_resumes_a_stopped_thread_rather_than_refusing_it`: `a_prompt_whose_turn_never_started_does_not_swallow_the_next_one` — `create(Some(cursor))`, `send("one")` (the fake provider emits nothing), `script.emit(SessionExited { code: None, expected: false })`, settle, `send("two")`, then `script.emit(TurnStarted { turn: T2, user_item })`, settle, and assert the projection contains an `ItemKind::UserMessage` whose text is `"two"`. It fails today: no user item is projected for the second send.
verify_reason: The code shape is exactly as quoted — manager.rs:421-423 is the only producer, manager.rs:784-792 the only head-matching consumer, and `grep -rn pending_claude_inputs crates/` returns just those two plus thread.rs:23/46 — so a non-matching head does block the deque permanently. What I could not prove is the trigger. In the real Claude adapter `TurnStarted` is emitted *synchronously inside* `send` (providers/claude/mod.rs:141-153, `begin_turn` at claude/map.rs:118-134) and `AgentSessionManager::send` holds `runtime.operation` from manager.rs:381 through the push at 421, while the event task takes that same lock per event (manager.rs:938), so the ordinary orderings all drain: a second send that lands before the drain reuses `inflight_turn` and coalesces into the same T1 (manager.rs:381-395 + `begin_turn` returning `None`), and a write failure returns `Err` before the push (claude/mod.rs:154-165). `stop` even synthesises a `TurnStarted` and drains explicitly for this exact case (manager.rs:601-620), which shows the author covered the known window. That leaves only (a) `store.append` failing at manager.rs:1020-1023 — after which every later append fails too, so the transcript is broken regardless — and (b) `stop` returning early on a provider-stop error (manager.rs:593-596, i.e. the race in agents-claude-stop-select-race-wedges-turn) skipping that drain while the supervisor's `SessionExited` clears `inflight_turn` at manager.rs:1031-1039. So the defect is real but reachable only through another defect or a disk failure; the failure scenario as written ("the reducer rejects it") I could not construct.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager.rs (`send`, `stop`, `drain_claude_inputs_applied_locked`, `apply_event`), crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/thread.rs (the deque field if it gains a turn-keyed shape), and crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager/tests.rs — the fake provider at tests.rs:179 emits no `TurnStarted` of its own, so any new flush-on-exit path changes the event stream several existing tests assert on (`stop_exits_the_session_and_refuses_later_sends` tests.rs:790, `send_resumes_a_stopped_thread_rather_than_refusing_it` tests.rs:1163, `a_crashed_provider_is_dropped_so_the_next_send_resumes_the_thread` tests.rs:1200).
corrected_fix: Do not `retain`/drop the stranded entries as proposed — those prompts were already written to Claude's stdin, so discarding them makes the transcript lie in the other direction (the model answers a prompt that is not there). Reuse the settlement the stop path already implements: factor manager.rs:601-620 into a `flush_pending_claude_inputs_locked(runtime)` that, for any turn still holding entries, appends a synthetic `TurnStarted` (only when the projection is not already `Running` on it) plus the drained user items, and call it from the same place `inflight_turn` is cleared (manager.rs:1031-1039) as well as from `stop`. Key the drain by turn (`extract_if`/partition on `pending_turn == turn`) rather than by head so a stale entry can never shadow a later one. Also fix manager.rs:593-596 (see the stop-race finding) so the existing drain is not skipped.

rule: rust-async-background-work / harness-protocols.md:731 "Child exit or stdout EOF … is runtime death" — a clean stop must not be reported as a provider failure
summary: When the child exits from the stdin close before the supervisor polls the queued `Stop` command, `select!` takes the `child.wait()` branch, drops the `done` oneshot, and `RunningProcess::stop` returns `ProviderError::Exited`, so `AgentSessionManager::stop` reports a conflict and skips every settlement it owes — leaving an in-flight turn `Running` forever.
failure_scenario: A Claude turn is streaming; the user presses stop. `RunningProcess::stop` sets `expected_stop`, closes stdin (`writer.close().await`), and `claude -p` exits on EOF during that round trip. `supervisor.send(Stop(done))` buffers into the capacity-2 channel, but the supervisor task is now woken with both branches ready and `select!` picks `child.wait()` at random; the task returns, `supervisor_receiver` and the queued `done` drop. `stop()` returns `Err(Exited { code: None })`, the user gets `conflict: agent provider exited: None` in the status bar, and because the manager returned early, no `TurnAborted` is appended. The supervisor's own `SessionExited { expected: true }` sets `session = Stopped` but `fail_active_turn` runs only for `expected: false` (projection.rs:442-450), so `TurnState::Running(turn)` persists — `attention()` returns `Working` forever (projection.rs:345-351) and the tab spins on a dead process until the daemon restarts.
proposed_fix: Make the exit path answer the pending stop instead of racing it: after the `child.wait()` branch fires, drain `supervisor_receiver` and reply `Ok(())` to any queued `Stop(done)` (or have `RunningProcess::stop` treat a dropped `done` as success once `expected_stop` is set, since the child is provably gone). Independently, make `AgentSessionManager::stop` settle the turn and session on the error path too, rather than returning before `settle_open_gates_locked`/`TurnAborted`/`SessionExited`.
test_plan: Add to `process.rs`'s test module: `stopping_a_child_that_already_exited_is_not_an_error` — spawn a trivial child (`/bin/cat` with piped stdio), `writer.close()`, wait for the supervisor's `SessionExited` to reach the sink, then call `RunningProcess::stop()` and assert `Ok(())`. Complement it in `manager/tests.rs` with `stop_settles_the_turn_even_when_the_provider_stop_fails`: make the fake provider's `stop()` return `Err(ProviderError::Exited { code: None })` while a turn is running, call `manager.stop(thread)`, and assert the projection's `turn` is `TurnState::Interrupted`/`Failed` rather than `Running`. Both fail today.
verify_reason: Every step checks out against the source. The `tokio::select!` at providers/claude/process.rs:352-383 has no `biased;`, so when the child has already exited and a `Stop` is queued both branches are ready and the arm is chosen at random; the `child.wait()` arm returns without touching `supervisor_receiver`, dropping the queued `Stop(done)`. `RunningProcess::stop` (process.rs:107-124) only falls back to `close_result` when `supervisor.send` itself fails (receiver already dropped); once the send has succeeded into the capacity-2 channel (process.rs:267) a dropped `done` becomes `ProviderError::Exited { code: None }` at process.rs:120-121. `AgentSessionManager::stop` (manager.rs:593-596) then restores the provider and returns, skipping `settle_open_gates_locked`, the synthesized `TurnStarted`+drain, the `TurnAborted` and the `SessionExited` at manager.rs:598-636. The supervisor meanwhile emits `SessionExited { expected: true }` (expected_stop was set at process.rs:108), and the reducer only calls `fail_active_turn` for `expected: false` (projection.rs:442-451), so `TurnState::Running(turn)` survives and `attention()` returns `Working` because the turn arm at projection.rs:345-351 fires before the session arm. Note the `Stop` arm itself handles an already-dead child fine (`terminate` at process.rs:493-499 returns immediately), so the branch choice really is the whole defect. The window is narrow — the child must be reaped before the supervisor is polled with the queued Stop — but it is exactly the shape of a stop pressed on a child that has just died.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/providers/claude/process.rs (supervisor task + `RunningProcess::stop`, and its `mod tests` at process.rs:577), crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager.rs `stop` (manager.rs:585-636) and crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager/tests.rs (`stop_exits_the_session_and_refuses_later_sends` tests.rs:790 asserts today's happy path; a fake `stop()` error case is new). Changing `stop` to settle on error also affects the OpenCode path, whose `ManagedServer::stop` (providers/opencode/server.rs) is the other real error source — check no test asserts the current `Err` propagation for it. Fixing this also removes the only non-storage trigger for agents-pending-claude-inputs-head-of-line.
corrected_fix: Two changes, both worth making. (1) In process.rs, close the race at its source rather than draining after the fact: add `biased;` to the `select!` so the command arm is always polled first, and in the `child.wait()` arm drain `supervisor_receiver` (`while let Ok(cmd) = supervisor_receiver.try_recv()`) answering any `Stop(done)` with `Ok(())` — the child is provably gone at that point. Draining alone without `biased;` still leaves the exit arm emitting `SessionExited` before the drain, which is fine, but `biased;` makes the common case deterministic. Do not adopt the alternative of treating a dropped `done` as success purely on `expected_stop`: that flag is set before `writer.close()`, so it would also mask a supervisor task that panicked. (2) In manager.rs:593-596, do not swallow the error but do not abort the settlement either: log at warn, drop the provider handle, and fall through to `settle_open_gates_locked` / `TurnAborted` / `SessionExited` / `abort_task`, returning the ack. A provider that cannot be killed is a diagnostic, not a reason to leave the transcript claiming a turn is still running.

rule: gpui-performance / NATIVE-AGENTS §5 "one event per item per ~16 ms" — the reducer's per-event cost must not be O(transcript)
summary: Every applied event deep-clones the entire `ThreadProjection` — items, turns, notices, checkpoints, gates and all their `String`/`Value` payloads — only so `update_record` can read `projection.title`.
failure_scenario: A long-running thread with a few thousand transcript items (tool inputs and outputs are `serde_json::Value` and `String`). The delta coalescer emits roughly one event per 16 ms tick (manager.rs:36, 927-937), so the daemon performs ~60 full deep clones of the whole transcript per second of streaming — tens of megabytes of allocation and copying per second on the operation-gated path that every other verb (`send`, `respond`, `stop`) has to queue behind. The cost grows linearly with the transcript, so the thread gets slower to stream the longer it lives.
proposed_fix: Reborrow the guard once and pass the field: `let state = &mut *state;` then `update_record(&mut state.record, &sequenced, &state.projection);` — disjoint field borrows make the clone unnecessary. If a narrower signature is preferred, pass `&str` (the title) instead of `&ThreadProjection`.
test_plan: Add `manager/tests.rs::applying_an_event_does_not_clone_the_transcript` as a cost assertion: build a thread with N=2_000 projected items, wrap the daemon home's allocator or (simpler, deterministic) assert on a counter — e.g. make `update_record` take `&str` and add a compile-level test that `apply_event` performs no `ThreadProjection::clone`, asserted by `#[deny]`-style review plus a criterion-free timing guard: apply 200 `ContentDelta` events to a 2_000-item projection and assert wall time under a generous bound (e.g. 200 ms) that the current O(n·m) clone blows past. The direct, non-flaky form is to instrument `ThreadProjection` with a `#[cfg(test)] static CLONES: AtomicUsize` bumped in a manual `Clone` impl and assert it stays at the two `summary()` calls' cost (zero projection clones) across 200 applied events.
verify_reason: manager.rs:1028-1030 clones the whole `ThreadProjection` and passes it to `update_record`, whose only use of it is `record.title.clone_from(&projection.title)` at manager.rs:1116-1117 — I read the rest of the function (manager.rs:1118-1150) and it touches only `event`. I also grepped the enclosing block: `projection` appears nowhere after line 1041, and `before`/`after` are built from `state.projection.summary(...)` directly (manager.rs:1004, 1044), so the clone is dead weight. `ThreadProjection` owns `items`, `turns`, `gates`, `checkpoints`, `notices` (projection.rs:135-186), all deep-cloned. The delta coalescer really does drive roughly one apply per `DELTA_TICK` (manager.rs:927-937), so the cost is O(transcript) per event, i.e. quadratic over a session — the same trap `ThreadProjection::apply`'s own comment (projection.rs:221-225) says it deliberately avoids by validating before mutating.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager.rs only — `update_record` is private and has this one call site. No test asserts on it; the suggested clone-counting test in the finding's test plan is not worth adding (it would require a hand-written `Clone` impl on a public core type just for instrumentation).
corrected_fix: The proposed reborrow is right and is the minimal change, but prefer narrowing the signature at the same time so the trap cannot come back: change `fn update_record(record: &mut AgentThreadRecord, event: &SeqEvent, title: &str)` and call it as `update_record(&mut state.record, &sequenced, &state.projection.title)` after `let state = &mut *state;` (the reborrow is required either way — `MutexGuard` deref means `&mut state.record` and `&state.projection` cannot both be taken through the guard). Delete the now-unused `let projection = ...` binding; keep `let previous = state.record.clone()`, which `index_metadata_changed` at manager.rs:1045 genuinely needs.

rule: NATIVE-AGENTS §2 as stated in this file's own comment (opencode/mod.rs:189-193): "a server configured to allow everything would still render `asks before edits` — a false statement of scope"
summary: `OpenCodeProvider::set_mode` records the requested mode verbatim, skipping the `effective_mode` downgrade `start` applies, so the metadata row can advertise a permission promise the server will never keep.
failure_scenario: An `opencode.json` whose `permission` block allows every action. `start` correctly reports `FullAccess` and the tab reads `full access`. The user switches to `Ask` from the palette: `set_mode(Ask)` stores `Ask`, the manager appends `MetadataChanged { mode: Some(Ask) }`, and the tab now reads `asks before edits`. The server still auto-allows everything, so no `permission.asked` ever arrives and no gate ever opens — the row states a scope that is false, which is exactly what the start path is written to prevent. The mapper's `AutoPermission` path is also disabled (map.rs:1279), so a gate that *did* arrive would now sit unanswered.
proposed_fix: Route `set_mode` through the same helper: `let mode = effective_mode(self.http()?, mode).await;` before storing it and telling the mapper, and return the effective mode to the manager (or have the manager read `provider`'s mode back) so `update_settings_locked` records what the tab may honestly show.
test_plan: Add to `opencode/tests.rs` beside the existing `effective_mode` coverage: `set_mode_reports_the_mode_the_server_will_actually_honour` — stand up the fake server with a `GET /config` whose permission block allows everything, `start` with `PermissionMode::Ask` (asserting the reported mode is `FullAccess`), then call `set_mode(PermissionMode::Ask)` and assert `provider.mode` / the mapper's mode is still `FullAccess`. It fails today: the mode drops back to `Ask`.
verify_reason: The asymmetry is exactly as described. `start` routes the requested mode through `effective_mode(&http, req.mode)` at providers/opencode/mod.rs:194 and stores the result (mod.rs:236 `self.mode = mode;`), with `effective_mode` (mod.rs:573-598) answering `FullAccess` whenever `permission_allows_everything()` is true; `set_mode` (mod.rs:386-393) assigns the caller's mode verbatim and hands the same unfiltered value to the mapper. The manager then persists the caller's value, not the provider's: manager.rs:527-529 calls `update_settings_locked(&runtime, Some(mode), None)` with the argument it was given. So on an allow-everything server the row goes from a true `full access` to a false `asks before edits` — precisely the failure the comment at mod.rs:188-193 says the start path exists to prevent. Severity is presentational only, which the finding slightly overstates: on such a server `permission.asked` never fires, so nothing is left unanswered; the mapper's `plan_approved` bookkeeping is unaffected.
blast_radius: The `AgentProvider` trait definition (crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/providers/mod.rs) and both implementors — providers/opencode/mod.rs:386 and providers/claude/mod.rs:184 — plus the fake in crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager/tests.rs:194, and the caller at manager.rs:516-533. `a_mode_change_is_a_durable_event_every_mirror_sees` (manager/tests.rs:943) asserts the persisted mode and must keep passing for a fake whose effective mode equals the requested one. New coverage belongs beside the existing `effective_mode` tests in the opencode test module.
corrected_fix: Route it through the same helper, but keep the failure mode `start` has: `let mode = match self.http() { Ok(http) => effective_mode(http, mode).await, Err(_) => mode };` — `self.http()?` as proposed would turn a mode switch on a not-yet-running session into a hard error, which `start`'s own 'a server that will not answer keeps the requested mode' rule rejects. The manager must then record what the provider settled on, not what the caller asked: the cleanest shape is to change the trait method to `async fn set_mode(&mut self, mode: PermissionMode) -> ProviderResult<PermissionMode>` and feed that return value into `update_settings_locked` at manager.rs:527-529; a `fn mode(&self) -> PermissionMode` accessor on the trait works too but leaves two sources of truth.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiable: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call; use `?`, log it, or match it — the one exception is a fire-and-forget channel send, which needs a comment"
summary: The `create` rollback discards the result of `provider.stop()`, so a provider that fails to stop after a failed index write leaves an orphaned `claude`/`opencode serve` child with no thread record, no log line and no way to reach it again.
failure_scenario: `AgentThreadCreate` on a full disk. `provider.start()` has already spawned `opencode serve` (or `claude -p`); `store.write_index` fails; the rollback calls `provider.stop()`, whose `signal_group` returns `EPERM` (the child re-parented into a group Fleet no longer owns) — `ProviderError::Protocol` is dropped on the floor. The caller sees only "native-agent storage failed", while an `opencode serve` keeps holding its loopback port and the worktree for the life of the machine. Nothing in the log names it, because the only diagnostic was the discarded `Err`.
proposed_fix: Match the error and log it, in the house style used elsewhere in this file: `if let Err(error) = provider.stop().await { tracing::warn!(%error, thread = %thread, "could not stop the provider after a failed index write"); }`. Same treatment for the four `let _ignored = server.stop(&self.events_tx).await` sites in `opencode/mod.rs:177,185,226,234` and the `let _ = process.writer.write(interrupt_message(..))` in `claude/mod.rs:217`.
test_plan: Add to `manager/tests.rs`: `a_failed_index_write_reports_a_provider_that_would_not_stop` — make the fake provider's `stop()` return `Err(ProviderError::Protocol { .. })` and make the store's index path unwritable (create `index.json` as a directory), then call `create` and assert with `tracing_test`/a capturing subscriber that a warn-level line naming the thread was emitted. It fails today because the error is discarded silently.
verify_reason: manager.rs:275-280 is a bare discard of a fallible call — `let _ignored = provider.stop().await;` — and the house rules name that exact form: .claude/skills/rust-async-background-work/SKILL.md:262 and references/patterns.md:563 list `let _ignored =` alongside `let _ =` as 'never, on a fallible call', and CLAUDE.md's exemption is only for a commented fire-and-forget channel send, which this is not. The error is genuinely producible: `RunningProcess::stop` returns `Protocol`/`Timeout`/`Exited` (providers/claude/process.rs:107-124) and the OpenCode server stop propagates a non-ESRCH signal failure. After the early return nothing else holds the handle — `runtime` is dropped and the thread was never inserted into `inner.threads` (that happens at manager.rs:281-285). The practical severity is lower than the finding implies: a log line does not reap the orphan, so the value here is diagnostic and rule-compliance, not recovery.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager.rs alone for the cited site. Skip the suggested `tracing_test` assertion — the daemon has no capturing-subscriber test helper today, and adding one plus an unwritable-index fixture is more machinery than the change deserves; the `create` failure path is already exercised by the existing storage-error tests.
corrected_fix: As proposed for this site — `if let Err(error) = provider.stop().await { tracing::warn!(target: "fleet::agents", %error, %thread, "could not stop the provider after a failed index write"); }`. Leave the four OpenCode `let _ignored = server.stop(&self.events_tx).await` sites (opencode/mod.rs:177,185,226,234) and claude/mod.rs:217 out of this change or make them a separate commit: they are on paths that already return a more informative error, and folding five unrelated files into a rollback fix violates the one-logical-change-per-commit rule in CLAUDE.md. If they are touched, they need the same warn-and-continue treatment, not `?`.

rule: rust-gpui-testing, Anti-patterns: "Polling a wall clock for a condition (timeout + sleep loop) — slow, load-sensitive, hides the real ordering bug"; checklist Determinism: "Is the test free of 'poll until true with a wall-clock deadline' loops?"
summary: The agent-manager suite drives every asynchronous assertion through a wall-clock `settle` loop (5 s deadline, 5 ms real sleeps) under an unpaused `#[tokio::test]`, although the crate already dev-depends on `tokio` with `test-util`.
failure_scenario: Under a loaded CI box (or `cargo test --workspace` running the 44 integration binaries in parallel), a thread that legitimately needs >5 s of scheduler time fails with `agent thread never reached …` — a flake indistinguishable from a real regression. Conversely, an ordering bug where the projection reaches the expected state *and then regresses* is invisible: `settle` returns on the first poll that matches and the 5 ms gaps hide the intermediate states entirely.
proposed_fix: Await the signal the manager already emits instead of polling: the manager broadcasts thread updates, so `settle` should subscribe to that receiver and `recv()` until the predicate holds, with no sleep. Where a genuine timer is under test, add `start_paused = true` and `tokio::time::advance`.
test_plan: Rewrite `settle` to `let mut updates = self.manager.subscribe(); loop { if predicate(&self.projection(thread).await) { return … } updates.recv().await.expect("manager update sender"); }` and delete `SETTLE`. Then add `a_thread_that_never_reaches_the_state_fails_instead_of_hanging` under `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]`. The regression guard: set the harness's script to emit nothing and assert the test fails deterministically rather than after 5 s of wall clock.
verify_reason: The facts check out: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager/tests.rs:363-381 is a `timeout(SETTLE=5s)` + 5 ms real-sleep poll under plain `#[tokio::test]`, with an open-coded duplicate at :1226-1240, and the skill names that anti-pattern explicitly. What I could not prove from the code is the harm: every call re-reads a projection from an in-process scripted provider, so the 5 s budget is enormous relative to the work, and I found no flake evidence in the repo. The 'intermediate states are invisible' argument is generic to any settle helper, event-driven or not. Downgraded because the claimed defect (flakiness / hidden ordering bug) is unproven, and because the fix's premise is wrong as written — there is no `manager.subscribe()`; the manager publishes through `BroadcastBus` (manager.rs:45, :1084-1089).
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager/tests.rs only — one `settle` helper, its 19 call sites keep their signature, plus the open-coded loop at :1226. No production code, provided the harness reuses the `BroadcastBus` it already constructs.
corrected_fix: If changed at all: the harness already builds the bus (`let events = BroadcastBus::new(1_024);`, tests.rs:306 — keep it in the struct alongside the existing `events: BroadcastBus` field at :243) so `settle` can hold `events.subscribe()` and `recv()` until an `Event::Agent`/`Event::AgentSummary` for that thread arrives, re-checking the predicate each time — with the 5 s `timeout` KEPT as a backstop, so a manager that publishes nothing still fails instead of hanging forever. Do NOT convert these to `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]`: the manager does real filesystem IO through `spawn_blocking` (manager.rs:340), and auto-advance treats a blocked blocking-pool task as idle, which turns a pause into spurious instant timeouts. Reserve `start_paused` for tests whose subject is a timer, as machines/link.rs:922 already does.

rule: NATIVE-AGENTS §5 via the reducer's own TokenUsage comment (projection.rs:676-680): "turn metadata is withheld until the turn completes, so the footer never moves under the reader"
summary: `settle_blocked_time` charges gate wait to a turn whose `ended` footer is already frozen, so answering OpenCode's plan gate retroactively shrinks the completed turn's duration, to zero when the user reads for longer than the turn ran.
failure_scenario: An OpenCode thread in plan mode. The turn runs 45 s, `session.idle` arrives: the reducer applies `GateOpened(plan, turn=T)` (blocked_since = now) then `TurnCompleted(T, duration_ms = 45_000)`. `turns[0].footer().duration_ms` is 45_000. The user reads the plan for two minutes and clicks Approve. `GateResolved` empties `gates`, so `settle_blocked_time(Some(T), since, at)` adds 120_000 to `T.blocked_ms`, and the same settled turn's footer now reads `45_000.saturating_sub(120_000) == 0` — the footer of a turn the user already read moves from `45s` to `0s`.
proposed_fix: In `settle_blocked_time`, skip a turn that has already settled: `if let Some(record) = self.turns.iter_mut().find(|r| r.id == owner && r.ended.is_none())`. A gate that outlives its turn is not time that turn spent working, so it must not be subtracted from a frozen footer.

The OpenCode mapper really does open the plan gate inside settlement and before the settle event: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/providers/opencode/map.rs:1389-1405 pushes `GateOpened { turn: Some(active.id), kind: GateKind::Plan }` and only then (map.rs:1432-1443) `TurnCompleted`. The reducer's `GateOpened` arm (projection.rs:623-635) stamps `blocked_since = ev.at`, and `GateResolved` (projection.rs:636-662) calls `settle_blocked_time(owner, since, ev.at)` with `owner = gates[index].turn`, i.e. the now-settled turn. Nothing clears or freezes gates at `TurnCompleted` (the only `self.gates` mutations are at projection.rs:631/634/655). The two existing blocked-time tests (projection.rs:1292-1340 `a_turn_footer_excludes_the_time_the_turn_stood_blocked_on_the_user`, 1343-1378 `overlapping_gates_are_one_wait_not_two`) both resolve the gate *before* `complete_turn`, and the only plan-gate resolution test (projection.rs:2466-2489) uses `turn: None` — so the settled-turn case is genuinely uncovered. The reducer's own §5 comment at projection.rs:676-680 states the invariant this violates.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-core/src/agents/projection.rs only (the `settle_blocked_time` body plus a new test beside projection.rs:1292 and 1343). No daemon or app change: `blocked_ms` is read only by `TurnRecord::footer`, and the wire type is unchanged, so no proto golden or snapshot moves.
corrected_fix: The `r.ended.is_none()` guard is safe (both existing tests resolve before settlement, so they keep passing) but it throws away the part of the wait that genuinely fell inside the turn when a gate straddles settlement. Prefer clamping the charge to the turn's own window inside `settle_blocked_time`: look the record up once, and when `record.ended` is `Some(end)`, charge `min(at, record.started_at + end.duration_ms) - since` (saturating to 0) instead of `at - since`; when `ended` is `None` keep today's behaviour. For the OpenCode plan gate — opened at settlement — that clamps to 0, which is the outcome the finding wants, while a permission gate answered a beat after an abort still keeps the seconds it really blocked. Do not instead try to freeze the footer by snapshotting `duration_ms` at `TurnCompleted`: `footer()` is the only reader and the subtraction is the intended design.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Shape and hygiene: "Do assertion helpers carry #[track_caller]? Without it the failure points at the helper, not the failing test."
summary: `assert_frame`, the golden-frame helper called ~30 times from a single test function, has no `#[track_caller]`, so any golden mismatch reports line 30 or 37 of the helper instead of the wire message that broke.
failure_scenario: Add a field to `RequestBody::CreateWorktree` without `#[serde(default)]`. `request_wire_goldens` fails with `assertion left == right failed, compatibility.rs:31` and a byte-slice diff of two 200-character JSON blobs — the reader has to count `assert_frame` calls to find which of the ~20 request variants broke. Since the same helper also serves the response and event goldens, the reported line is identical for every one of the three tests.
proposed_fix: Put `#[track_caller]` on `assert_frame` (and on the equivalent helpers in `crates/fleet-core/tests/compatibility.rs`), and add `pretty_assertions` to `[workspace.dependencies]` as a dev-dependency so the byte-slice diff is readable.
test_plan: Temporarily change one golden literal in `request_wire_goldens` (e.g. `"protocol":7` → `"protocol":8`) and run `cargo test -p fleet-proto --test compatibility`. Before the fix the panic location is `crates/fleet-proto/tests/compatibility.rs:31`; after adding `#[track_caller]` it is the `assert_frame(…)` call site inside `request_wire_goldens`. Revert the literal.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-proto/tests/compatibility.rs:23-38 defines `assert_frame` with three `assert_eq!`s and no `#[track_caller]`, and it is the sole assertion vehicle for `request_wire_goldens` (:41), `response_wire_goldens` (:174) and `event_wire_goldens` (:321) — every golden mismatch in any of the three reports line 30, 31 or 36. `grep -rn track_caller crates/` confirms all eight existing uses are in fleet-ui-kit production helpers, none on a test helper.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-proto/tests/compatibility.rs only — one attribute, no signature or call-site change.
corrected_fix: Add `#[track_caller]` to `assert_frame` and nothing else. Drop both extras from the proposal: crates/fleet-core/tests/compatibility.rs has no assertion helper (its five tests assert inline), so there is nothing there to annotate; and adding `pretty_assertions` to `[workspace.dependencies]` is unrelated scope — a new workspace dependency edge is a separate decision under the workspace-architecture rules, and byte-slice readability is better served by comparing `str::from_utf8_lossy(&frame[4..])` against `golden` inside the helper.
